Matholwch leaves the court in anger, and Bendigeidfran's first messengers bring back only his complaint; a second embassy, led by Manawydan, offers him a sound horse for every one maimed, a rod of silver as tall as himself and a plate of gold as broad as his face, and peace on his own terms. Matholwch's council judges that refusal would bring more shame than redress, and he returns; when he sits sullen at the feast, Bendigeidfran adds a cauldron that brings the slain back to life by morning, though they cannot speak. On the second night Matholwch asks where the cauldron came from, and tells the story of the giant Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid and his still bigger wife Cymidei Cymeinfoll, who came out of the Lake of the Cauldron in Ireland, made themselves hated, and escaped from an iron house heated white around them, to come over to Britain and settle.
